title: Disagreement-routed selective querying of matched-capacity compact teachers
question: When compact training can query a cheap low-capacity or an expensive high-capacity 2D-Gaussian teacher per tile, does routing by precomputed inter-teacher disagreement reach matched held-out risk against the high-capacity teacher at materially lower query cost than always querying the high-capacity teacher?
hypothesis: Routing low-disagreement tiles to the 640-component teacher and high-disagreement tiles to the 2000-component teacher, with a random audit fraction querying both, reaches the matched held-out risk (evaluated against the high-capacity fields only) with a substantially cheaper query mix than always-high-capacity, while random routing at the same query-budget split loses quality, proving the disagreement signal carries the routing value.
claim_boundary: Development evidence for teacher-query routing efficiency inside the RGB-free compact trainer on the two development-exposed stage frames, conditional on a profiling gate showing teacher queries are a material share of step time. Held-out risk is always evaluated against the high-capacity teacher fields; the low-capacity tier is a query-cost lever, never the evaluation authority. It establishes no claim about teacher-capacity quality itself, no cross-scene generality, and no production default change.

stages.label: Load matched dual teachers
stages.purpose: Load the sealed low- and high-capacity 2D Gaussian bundles for identical views and verify both against the data seal; no image-capable loader.

stages.label: Precompute tile disagreement
stages.purpose: Compute one low-resolution per-view, per-tile expected discrepancy between the two teacher tiers directly from compact fields, once, before optimization.

stages.label: Shared frozen initialization
stages.purpose: Construct one hash-verified 3D initialization used identically by every cell so only the routing policy differs.

stages.label: Routed compact optimization
stages.purpose: Run the RGB-free compact trainer with per-tile teacher routing under the cell's policy; the audit fraction queries both tiers on the same points and records their divergence.

stages.label: Held-out evaluation against the high-capacity teacher
stages.purpose: Evaluate every cell on identical held-out fields of the high-capacity teacher only, at matched budgets and at the matched-risk stopping point.

stages.label: Routing audit reconciliation
stages.purpose: Reconcile audit-fraction double queries into misroute and staleness rates so incorrect routing is detected rather than silently absorbed.

comparators.label: Always query the 2000-component teacher
comparators.purpose: The quality anchor and current implicit policy; all risk targets are defined against this cell's teacher fields.

comparators.label: Always query the 640-component teacher
comparators.purpose: Cheap-only floor; bounds how much quality the low tier alone can support.

comparators.label: Disagreement-thresholded routing with audit fraction
comparators.purpose: The treatment: cheap teacher on low-disagreement tiles, expensive teacher on high-disagreement tiles, random audit fraction querying both.

comparators.label: Random routing at the matched query split
comparators.purpose: Same cheap/expensive query-budget split as the routed cell with random tile assignment; isolates the disagreement signal from the mere budget mix.

primary_metrics.label: Wall time to matched held-out risk
primary_metrics.aggregation: paired median over measured repeats, seeds, and scenes at the frozen risk target

primary_metrics.label: High-capacity teacher queries
primary_metrics.aggregation: paired median over seeds and scenes at the matched-risk stopping point

primary_metrics.label: Low-capacity teacher queries
primary_metrics.aggregation: paired median over seeds and scenes at the matched-risk stopping point

primary_metrics.label: Held-out pixel risk versus the high-capacity teacher
primary_metrics.aggregation: median per view, then paired median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Held-out area risk versus the high-capacity teacher
primary_metrics.aggregation: median per view, then paired median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Audit-detected misroute rate
primary_metrics.aggregation: fraction of audited tiles whose observed divergence contradicts their routing class; median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Teacher-query share of step time
primary_metrics.aggregation: profiled share of optimization step time spent in teacher queries per cell; median over seeds and scenes

resource_protocol.scope: fresh reconstruction-only process from compact manifest open through final PLY save; disagreement precompute and audit double-queries are inside the measured boundary so routing pays for its own overhead
resource_protocol.aggregation: paired median on one idle named GPU; retain every raw repeat and report min/max

blockers: Profiling gate first: measure the share of compact-training step time spent in high-capacity teacher queries at the frozen production settings and record the receipt; this task proceeds to implementation only if that share exceeds a threshold frozen before profiling (proposal: 20%). If the gate fails, close this task as not-worth-it with the profile as evidence.

Produce and seal matched 640-component and 2000-component teacher bundles for both frames under one identical fitting configuration with production manifests, then update the datasets and data_seal to the new seal before setting status to ready; the current seal covers only the existing bundles.

Implement the tile-disagreement precompute, threshold routing, and audit-fraction double-querying behind an opt-in compact-trainer config whose default preserves single-teacher behavior, with CPU-first tests for routing determinism, audit accounting, and misroute detection on a tiny fixture.

Freeze the routing threshold, audit fraction, tile size, matched held-out risk target, stopping rule, shared initialization artifact and hash, and the exact argv command before setting status to ready.
Freeze the CUDA host, GPU identity, and idle policy.
Assign a frozen owner and obtain a distinct outcome-unseen prospective protocol review.
